paper.title: Algorithm 762: LLDRLF, log-likelihood and some derivatives for log-F models (collected algorithm; title from the frame item)
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 22(3), 372-382 (Sep 1996); collected as ACM TOMS Algorithm 762
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/762.gz (ACM article not read; no ACM fetch attempted this wake)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 762.gz (fetched by scout 2026-11-27 09:58Z into a fresh /tmp directory; unpacked as text with sed line ranges and not executed)
code.note: Shell archive with members Doc/readme, Src/src.f (LLDRLF with double precision BRATIO), Drivers/driver1.f (program tstsht, defaults), Drivers/driver2.f (tstlld, all paper cases) and the shipped output RES1 (from driver1.f on an IBM RS6000/550, defaults). The claim uses RES1, which is a text member of the archive. Its member text has a few corrupted exponents (for example '-4.0378048673939815-308' in a log(1-F) line); the claim uses only the clean first block.

field: numerics (special functions and statistics: log-F likelihood)

claim.location: Shipped output RES1 of driver1.f, first block (A: 1.0000E-03, B: 1.0000E-03, Standard Deviation 1414.2147), the line 'log(f(exp(W)|DFN,DFD))' at W (in standard deviations) = -1000.0000 (line 8 of RES1).
claim.metric: log(f(exp(W)|DFN,DFD)) for W = -1000 standard deviations, A = B = 1e-3, as printed by LLDRLF through driver1.f (E-format, 17 significant digits).
claim.paper_value: The paper's own tables are not read. The value is the shipped RES1 output of driver1.f with defaults.

tolerance.basis: The value is about -1418.0, a double precision result. A relative tolerance of about 7e-10 accepts last-digit differences from a different compiler or BRATIO build and rejects any real change to the formula. It is fixed now, before any run, and not to be loosened after a run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: driver1.f evaluates a short grid of (A, B, W) cases.
cost.data_size: Under 1 MB: the archive is about 10 KB compressed and generates its own inputs.
cost.data_licence: No data beyond the archive. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The shipped driver computes LLDRLF in double precision on defined inputs and prints the log-density values, so a rerun must reproduce a deterministic floating-point value to the tolerance; the value is not a closed form.
